notice: NOT ORIGINAL DATA. None of the text in this file comes from the game's files; only the bank, film and clip names do.
Titanic: Adventure Out of Time voices these clips and never prints them. This is our best-effort transcript of the audio, made so that a player who cannot hear them can read them (#50).

Each 'text' was produced by speech recognition (Whisper large-v3-turbo, run locally on the English edition's sound banks) and then corrected by hand: names the recogniser cannot know (Zeitel, the Rubaiyat, Willie), and plain mishearings.
'heard' is what the recogniser wrote, kept wherever the text differs from it. 'guess': true marks a line whose wording is uncertain even after correction.

'who' names the speaker, shown before the words because captions can be up together (the radio and the landlady). The names were assigned from the lines' content and the clips' names; correct them by ear too.

'speakers' names who says the lines read from the game's own puppets (the ending, the films' voice-overs), by puppet file, or by puppet#line where one puppet holds several voices. Assigned by us, not the game. A puppet that seats two people in one close-up (wilzeit1.pup: Zeitel on the left, Willie on the right; shahack1.pup and shahack2.pup: Jack on the left, Shailagh on the right) says in each line's stance whose mouth moves, and the close-up shows it, so a line said there is captioned without a name. A name is only needed where a film plays a puppet's line, and the films' lines from these puppets are voice-overs that move neither face: wilzeit1.pup's are the gymnasium tour (tour3.mov), Willie's, who greets you there with his own mouth (wilfenc1.72) (#479).

'tracks' are looping tracks that talk, timed in seconds from the start of the loop as the engine assembles it: the bedsit radio's first station reads the news, and the gramophone in Carlson's trunk (oldboss.trk, cabin C-73) plays the service's briefing (#471), transcribed the same way and not yet checked by ear.

A caption in square brackets is not words but a sound that tells the player something they would otherwise miss, as subtitles for the deaf and hard of hearing do: the air-raid siren over the London flat (bedsit1.trk's track, #470), after which the room cannot be used. It names no speaker. Captions cover what is said and such sounds, not every sound in the game.
'films' are clips a film keeps in its own sound table and no puppet holds the words of: the narration over the opening credits (ocredits.mov). Transcribed the same way, from the film.
'listened': true marks a line someone has checked by ear. Where it is missing, the line is only as good as the recogniser and the context.
Corrections are welcome, and should be made by listening to the clip, not by editing the wording: the caption editor (taoot/captions/) plays every clip.
made: 2026-10-03, Whisper large-v3-turbo (int8, CPU), English; German for the fencing master, who speaks German in the English edition

z3.03.text: The Rubaiyat. It was not at your drop point.
z3.03.heard: The ruby aunt, it was not at your drop point.

z3.06.text: But I put it there myself. What happened?
z3.06.heard: But I put it there myself, of what happened.

z3.07.text: There's a third party on board. An agent working against you. Against us.

z3.09.text: My servant saw them at the drop.

z3.10.heard: They now have the ruby art.

z3.11.text: This could ruin me, Zeitel, if I were found out.
z3.11.heard: This could ruin me, Seidel, if I were found out.

z2.01.text: The drop. It worked as you said. I have it. The Rubaiyat's mine.
z2.01.heard: The drop. It worked as you said. I have it. The Rubiot's mine.

z2.03.text: More so the profit it brings.
z2.03.heard: more so the profit it brings.

z2.04.text: What will you do with it?

z2.05.text: There's an American tycoon who collects rare manuscripts. He'll pay a fortune and ask no questions.

z2.06.text: But there's just one problem, Colonel.

z2.08.text: There's a third party on board. An agent working against you. Against us.

z2.10.text: My servant who retrieved the Rubaiyat encountered them.
z2.10.heard: My servant who retrieved the rubyat encountered them.

z1.02.text: What about the painting? Did your associate bring it up from the cargo hold?

z1.04.text: No? But I put it there myself!

z1.05.text: Sasha, I've discovered a traitor. Don't look so startled. It is not you.

z1.07.text: No longer my associate, I am afraid.

z1.09.text: Willie was an intellectual, and intellectuals aren't smart enough for espionage.

z1.10.text: Now, I must recover the painting, and its plans. I fear this third party may already have possession of it.

z1.12.text: Thank you for asking. Willie will bring no further harm to the Fatherland, I assure you.
z1.12.heard: Thank you for asking, Billy will bring no further harm to the fatherland, I assure you.

door1.text: Sneaking out, are ya? I want me money!

door2.text: They said you was important once. Not now. You're just old, old and broke.

door3.text: When do I get me money?! When?!

lady2.text: About time, you're awake. You're two weeks late with the rent.
lady2.heard: Mom, you're awake. You're two weeks late with the rent.

lady3.text: War or no war, a tenant in arrears is not a tenant I'll put up with.
lady3.heard: War or no war, a tenant in a raise is not a tenant I'll put up with.

lady4.text: You don't pay by today, it's the street, I promise!

shay.jack.text: Jack, is that you? I'll be right out.

voice.1.text: The past, forever locked in regret. But what if the past could be changed?

voice.2.text: Thirty years have come and gone since the night that saw the end of a world, my world. The service needed someone on the Titanic. They chose me.

voice.3.text: I was to wait for a signal from my contact, so I remained in my cabin. I left only once: Georgia was on board.

voice.4.text: And that's when it came. There'd be no second chance. It was Sunday, April 14th. Too late, you see. For the Titanic. For me.

voice.5.text: What if I'd met with my contact? Prevented disaster. What if the past could be changed? What then?

bedrad1.trk.text: London has endured another night of German bombing.
Most damage was concentrated in the East End.
The RAF has struck enemy aerodromes in Le Havre and the Low Countries.
bedrad1.trk.heard: The RAF has struck enemy aerodromes in La Havre and the Low Countries.

bedrad1.trk.text: In Russia, further German losses are reported around Leningrad.
In Asia, the American fortress at Corregidor is still defiant,
but Japanese forces are reported nearing the Burmese oil fields.
And that concludes the news summary.
We now return you to our music program.

oldboss.trk.text: His Majesty's government has assigned an agent of the Crown to rendezvous with you on board the Titanic.
Remain in your cabin until your contact gives you further instructions.
After completion of all your assignments on board,
book passage to remain on the ship and return to Southampton for your next assignment.
For a more in-depth report of the international situation in the spring of 1912,
please review the white paper included as part of this briefing.
